solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Posh females and others in pub that serves food

indicators.note: the clue's other pieces are placed inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a pub is a bar
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
F is the abbreviation for female; FF doubles it for the plural
etc. (et cetera) means and others

explanation.surface: Smart women and their companions gather in a gastropub.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet car is the railway carriage where meals and snacks are sold to passengers.

clue.text: Black knight pens song for Scottish child

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the first pair of letters holds the song between them

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
N is the chess notation for a knight
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A villainous knight in black locks away a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scots word for a youngster or infant.

clue.text: Smoke keeps breathing organ working in Chinese system

indicators.note: the cigarette word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
the lung is the organ of breathing
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A smoker's cigarette keeps their lungs going inside some Chinese regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Falun Gong is a Chinese spiritual practice of meditation and exercises, banned by the state.

clue.text: Moth circles round American helicopter

indicators.note: to circle is to go around, so the moth's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: the eggar or egger is a family of moths, such as the oak eggar
a beat is a policeman's regular round

explanation.surface: A moth flutters in circles around a US chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggbeater is American slang for a helicopter, from its whirring rotor blades.

clue.text: In this way, one's sure to have an impact

definitions.text: In this way, one's sure to have an impact

parts.words: In this way, one's sure to have an impact
parts.note: having an impact sounds like making a mark, but here it is a literal crash: the heading two vehicles take when they must hit

explanation.surface: Advice on how to make a strong impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Two moving things on paths that must meet are heading for a crash, which is a literal impact.

clue.text: Might it be that sister? Poor nun in trouble!

definitions.note: the word 'that' is an example of the part of speech, as in 'the book that I read'

parts.note: a sister is a relative

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are in disarray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a struggling nun is that sister of theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sister' looks like a nun's title but simply means a family member; 'that' is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like who, which and that introduce a clause describing a noun, which is the grammatical class named.

clue.text: Reminder about university being complacent

indicators.note: the reminder word goes around the university letter

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder

explanation.surface: A nudge about one's university reveals smugness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pleased with oneself to excess, self-satisfied, is a sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Verifying which six must leave tip?

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for six has to go, being taken out of the word for verifying

parts.note: proving means verifying
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Checking which of six points has to be removed from a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a pointed tine, such as one of a fork's points; the question mark admits it is only one sort of tip.

clue.text: Piano used in old time musical presentation

indicators.note: the piano letter is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: an era is a period of time
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano features in an old-time music hall show.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, so a musical presentation.

clue.text: Tummy trouble in dreadful days without drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the shuffled letters sit outside the drink
dreadful signals that the letters of the word are in a terrible state, rearranged

parts.note: Pepsi is a brand of soft drink

explanation.surface: Someone suffers stomach pain after awful days with nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' suggests lacking, but here is the old sense of outside: DYSA, made by 'dreadful', goes round the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, an upset stomach.

clue.text: Sick bird sounded wrong

indicators.note: the pair of words, when spoken, give a word with a different spelling

parts.note: ill means sick; an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: An ailing bird's call sounds off-key.
explanation.definitionFit: Something against the law is unlawful, so wrong in a legal sense.

clue.text: With pride, she loses in brawling

definitions.note: a pride is a group of lions, and the female member is meant

indicators.note: the letters are fighting and scrambled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A proud woman refuses to back down and loses a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like the emotion but is the collective noun for lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A female lion lives in a pride, the group that lions form.

clue.text: Design on cent's piece coined for particular occasion

indicators.note: a piece of the words is taken, the run of letters lying across them

explanation.surface: The design on a cent coin was minted for a special event.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonce word is one invented for a single use, for one occasion only.

clue.text: Where coals are not hot, mix with others

indicators.note: not says the letter for hot is to be left out of the phrase

parts.note: coals burn in the grate of a fireplace
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Advice to join in with the crowd when the fire has gone cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to join in and become part of a wider community or group.

clue.text: Snake in alien surroundings — through water it sped

indicators.note: the alien's letters provide the surroundings for the snake

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial
a boa is a large snake

explanation.surface: A snake in strange surroundings swims fast through water.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a fast German motor torpedo boat of the Second World War.

clue.text: Former wife involved in dancing this reel

indicators.note: the wife letter is involved, wrapped up, inside the rearranged letters
the letters are dancing about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's ex-wife joins in dancing a Scottish reel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges THIS REEL and 'involved in' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile is an adjective for what once was, as in an erstwhile friend.

clue.text: Northern location where cool writer joins ship

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
Jules Verne was the French writer of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A trendy author boards a ship bound for the north.
explanation.walkthrough: INVERNESS is a city in the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is a Highland city in the north of Scotland, so a place in the north.

clue.text: Trouble keeping English quiet in governmental sort-out

indicators.note: the word for trouble keeps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to ruffle is to disturb or trouble
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Unrest keeps the English silent during a political shake-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reshuffle is a reorganisation of government posts by a prime minister.

clue.text: Oil producers lie and cut pay anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a disorderly way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oil companies tell lies and slash wages without care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producers' suggests petroleum firms; it means trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees are the source of eucalyptus oil, so they produce oil.

clue.text: Sweetheart given break to find mangetout

parts.note: sugar is a term of endearment, like sweetheart
to snap is to break

explanation.surface: A lover is given time off to go hunting vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout is a pea eaten pod and all, and the sugar snap is one such variety.

clue.text: Bones in bag next to top drawer?

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like part
RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist of the highest rank, a top drawer of pictures

explanation.surface: Bones are stored in a bag beside the top drawer of a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture but is one who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacra is the plural of sacrum, the triangular bone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Server misses one playing pool game

indicators.note: misses means goes without, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: a waiter serves food
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letters are playing about, rearranged

explanation.surface: A barman skips a shot while playing pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Water polo is a team sport played by swimmers with a ball in a pool.

clue.text: Cheap booze, no good, upset teacher

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top
no says the letter for good is to be removed

parts.note: rotgut is slang for cheap, poor-quality liquor

explanation.surface: A teacher is upset by drinking bad cheap alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing G from ROTGUT gives ROTUT, which 'upset' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or instructor.

clue.text: Rascal having non-British accent

indicators.note: non- means without, so the letter for British is taken away

parts.note: a brogue is a regional accent, especially Irish

explanation.surface: A scoundrel speaks with a foreign accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a scoundrel or mischievous person.

clue.text: Learner in military group not exactly bright

indicators.note: the learner letter goes inside the military group

parts.note: a unit is a military group
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A recruit in the army squad is not very clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bright' suggests clever, but means lit up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without light is dark, so hardly bright in the sense of illuminated.

clue.text: Under emotional pressure in past?

definitions.meaning: the past is a grammatical form of verbs, one example of the kind

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about events in their past.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means anxious and strained; in grammar it is the verb form for time, such as past or present.

clue.text: Maybe two for one in Bury

indicators.note: the example abbreviation goes inside the word for bury

parts.note: to inter is to bury
eg (for example) means for one

explanation.surface: Perhaps two people for each one buried in the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town near Manchester, which the capital disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is an example of a whole number, so the question 'maybe' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Not keen on what some doctors do in delivery method

parts.note: to be off something is to have lost one's liking for it
spin doctors put a favourable spin on news

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes how some doctors handle the birth of a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests childbirth but is a ball bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-spin is a style of bowling in cricket in which the ball is turned with the fingers.

clue.text: Eponymous heroine saves island home for birds

indicators.note: to save is to keep, so the heroine's name holds the island letter

parts.note: Jane Eyre is the title heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel

explanation.surface: A storybook heroine rescues an island bird sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, built high up.

clue.text: Comic, Eagle, keeping one enlightened

indicators.note: the eagle's name keeps the letter for one inside it

parts.note: the erne is the sea eagle
I is the Roman numeral for one
wise means enlightened, knowing

explanation.surface: A comic paper called Eagle keeps one reader informed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was a British comedian, half of the double act Morecambe and Wise; Eagle was also a British comic paper.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a famous British comedian, so a comic in the sense of a person who makes people laugh.
